comments.text: The gore can't get immersed in water and stay dry. I've tested it. But it doesn't leak as bad as you'd think. If you coat the gore with several layers of sealant it's very hard for water to get through, but that's not really necessary if you're just looking to be protected from rain and snow. I think Blunnies are a bit dorky, but this style of boot makes an excellent town boot for rainy days or northern winters. They're super comfortable and more than weather-proof enough. I really only wear mine in winter or in the rain, but they've lasted 15 years and still look almost new. If it's just to get you around town, you don't need the insulated ones. They're heavier and hotter and the regular ones are more versatile. I hate clunking around in winter boots because most of the time you're driving or otherwise inside. Just wear some wool socks if it's super cold out.
